newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China President Jiang expected at HK handover - radio.
newsitem.headline: China President Jiang expected at HK handover - radio.

text.p: Chinese President and Communist Party boss Jiang Zemin is expected to visit Hong Kong for the British colony's handover to China, Hong Kong government-run radio said on Thursday.
The radio said Jiang was expected to join heir to the British throne Prince Charles as the two main participants in the handover ceremony, set to take place at midnight on June 30.

There was no immediate official confirmation Jinag would come. But Hugh Davies, British delegation leader to the final round of diplomatic talks on the handover, told reporters China was expected to be represented at the most senior level.
"We've already announced that our principal participant will be the Prince of Wales," Davies said as he entered the second day of the talks on Thursday.
"We still await confirmation of who will be the principal participant on the Chinese side, although we've been given some broad hints that it's somebody very senior," he said.

If Jiang comes, it will be the first time a Chinese head of state, or any Communist head of state from any country, has set foot in Hong Kong, a bastion of capitalism since Britain seized it from the Manchu dynasty of imperial China in 1841.
